research_question: What is the effect of perioperative levosimendan compared with placebo on all-cause mortality in adults undergoing cardiac surgery?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality (deaths from any cause) reported as number of deaths and total number randomized in each arm; includes in-hospital, 30-day, and longest reported follow-up mortality.
positive_direction: A positive effect size (RR < 1 expressed in the favorable direction) means levosimendan reduced all-cause mortality compared with placebo — fewer deaths in the levosimendan arm.
search_queries: levosimendan cardiac surgery randomized placebo mortality
levosimendan coronary artery bypass grafting trial outcome
levosimendan valve surgery cardiopulmonary bypass controlled trial death
inclusion_criteria: Adult patients (≥18 years) undergoing any type of cardiac surgery
Compares levosimendan with placebo (or a no-levosimendan control) in any perioperative setting
Reports any quantitative mortality or clinical outcome data, including counts of deaths per arm
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a levosimendan (treatment) group and a placebo/control group
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts and arm sizes, means+SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds/risk ratios)
Completely unrelated to levosimendan in adult cardiac surgery (e.g., non-cardiac surgery, pediatric populations only, non-surgical heart failure only, animal or in vitro studies)
moderators_to_extract: Type of cardiac surgery (CABG, valve, combined/mixed)
Baseline left ventricular ejection fraction category (reduced vs preserved)
Timing of levosimendan initiation (preoperative vs intraoperative/postoperative)
Levosimendan dosing regimen (bolus plus infusion vs infusion only, total dose)
Risk of bias / blinding status and single- vs multi-center design
effect_size_note: Pool as a Risk Ratio (RR) using each trial's reported number of deaths and total randomized participants per arm (intention-to-treat denominators where available). Trials with zero deaths in BOTH arms are double-zero studies that contribute no information to an RR and must be treated as not estimable and excluded from the pooled estimate rather than continuity-corrected; at least three such trials are expected and they should still be listed in the study table with their counts. Single-zero trials (zero deaths in one arm only) retain the standard 0.5 continuity correction. Use a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) with Mantel-Haenszel weighting as a sensitivity check; report I² and a sensitivity analysis using Peto OR given the low event rates.
